transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Samir Cortez (Redwood SE), Amina Patel (Blue Moor CISO), Ethan Ross (Blue Moor SecEng), Lena Gomez (Blue Moor CTO), Marco Diaz (Blue Moor DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um we wanted to walk through the recent pen test and make sure our remediation plan and your tracking aligns with Blue Moor's compliance needs, uh Amina, thanks for making time
[00:12] Amina Patel: yeah thanks Jordan, big thing for us is making sure we have predictable remediation SLAs and also that any evidence you provide can be redacted for our vendors and compliance team, ok?
[00:22] Priya Nambiar: totally, we'll send a redacted version. quick note up-front, some of the vuln ids were environment specific - there are a couple of findings from the hosted infra that don't apply to your private deployment but we'll call those out
[00:34] Ethan Ross: okay that helps. first question — of the critical items in the report, how many are code-level vs infra config?
[00:40] Samir Cortez: rough split from our side was three criticals were infra-level (misconfigured bucket ACL, outdated container runtime, exposed admin port), two high were dependency CVEs pulled in by a transitive library in the ingestion pipeline
[00:52] Marco Diaz: that ingestion pipeline is ours — can you point to the CVE ids? we need to triage with our SREs
[00:58] Priya Nambiar: yes, we'll include the CVE list in the spreadsheet; I think the two high items are CVE-2026-1148 and CVE-2026-2210 (note: transcription may garble numbers), and they map to a third-party parser lib
[01:12] Lena Gomez: two things —1) we need to make sure this aligns to our SBOM and comp rules and 2) what's the expected patch cadence for these dependency fixes?
[01:20] Jordan Lee: good call. on patch cadence — Redwood recommends a tiered SLA: critical (CVSS 9-10) patches 72 hours remediation window for POCs/hosted customers, 5 business days for dedicated/private by policy but we can contractually tighten that; high (7-8.9) 7-14 days depending on exploitability; medium 30 days. that's what we usually present as a baseline
[01:41] Amina Patel: 72 hours for critical is fine but we need an emergency hotfix playbook. how do you handle emergency rollouts and rollback safety?
[01:48] Priya Nambiar: we use staged rollouts with canary shards, automated health checks and auto rollback on anomaly detection. for private deployments we can coordinate a runway with your ops team so rollouts happen in maintenance windows — there is also an emergency patch path if the vulnerability is zero-day exploited
[02:06] Ethan Ross: what's the instrumentation for the health checks? we need to see metrics and logs to validate a rollback condition
[02:12] Samir Cortez: health hooks feed into our console; you can see error rates, latency spikes, and we also stream audit events. we can set a pre-agreed SLO threshold for auto rollback and provide a log export for each rollout
[02:26] Marco Diaz: about audit logs — retention, format, and who owns the logs? we can't have vendor access to raw PII data in logs
[02:33] Jordan Lee: logs are shipped to a customer-owned destination for private deployments. by default hosted keeps 90 days, but for enterprise we can increase retention and route to your SIEM via secure forwarder. we redact PII at ingestion where applicable and can provide hashed identifiers instead
[02:47] Amina Patel: is there a separation of duties? RBAC model wise — can we limit who in Redwood can see trace-level data?
[02:54] Priya Nambiar: yes, RBAC is tenant-scoped. we have roles (viewer, operator, admin) and we can create custom roles. for private deployments, you control the role bindings; for hosted we enforce least privilege and offer audits of who accessed what via the audit log
[03:09] Lena Gomez: SSO — we need SAML with our IdP, and also SCIM for user provisioning. we also want MFA enforced for all admin roles
[03:17] Samir Cortez: supported. Redwood supports SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning; MFA is enforced for admin by default and can be required org-wide
[03:24] Ethan Ross: about encryption at rest — we need customer-managed keys, ideally HSM-backed. can you describe KMS options and HSM support?
[03:31] Priya Nambiar: sure. hosted customers can opt into BYOK (bring your own key) via a KMS integration with major cloud KMS providers, and for Private we support direct HSM integrations or a KMS proxy that points to your HSM. we also have envelope encryption so you control the CMK and Redwood only holds the wrapped DEKs
[03:47] Marco Diaz: any difference in key rotation or backup access for disaster recovery? we need a documented flow for rotating keys without bringing services down
[03:54] Priya Nambiar: yes, we support non-disruptive rotation patterns — double-wrapping DEKs during rotation and a backup key hierarchy. we'll provide the runbook in the follow-up deep dive
[04:05] Amina Patel: can you confirm what gets encrypted: model weights, logs, payloads in transit and at rest? we have to ensure certain artifacts are always encrypted for our regulators
[04:13] Jordan Lee: short answer: at-rest and in-transit are encrypted. model artifacts and persistent storage are encrypted with CMKs when BYOK enabled. transient memory in GPU nodes is harder to guarantee for customers, but we minimize exposure via ephemeral nodes and strict tenancy isolation in dedicated/private deployments
[04:30] Ethan Ross: ok noted. now the pen test — any false positives we should be aware of?
[04:35] Priya Nambiar: a couple of SCA (software composition analysis) flags were false positives due to backported patches we applied; the report will annotate those. also the exposed admin port was on a management plane that doesn't serve customer traffic — we'll mark that as out-of-scope in the redaction
[04:52] Lena Gomez: how do you track remediation and hand off proof for auditors? we need a ticketed trail with PRs and CVE closure evidence
[04:59] Samir Cortez: we can provide a remediation tracker spreadsheet and also export of relevant Jira tickets if we integrate into your issue tracker via API. for auditors we can bundle evidence: PR links, deploy timestamps, and test run outputs
[05:11] Amina Patel: SOC 2 and ISO — do you have recent attestations and can you share the control mappings?
[05:16] Jordan Lee: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II report from 2026 Q2 and ISO 27001 certification — we'll share summary artifacts and a control mapping doc that maps our controls to common frameworks. we'll need an NDA or secure upload for the full reports
[05:29] Ethan Ross: metadata: data residency — our primary data must remain in EU regions, can Redwood guarantee region locking for Blue Moor?
[05:37] Priya Nambiar: absolutely. for private deployments we can pin region and network egress policies. for hosted customers, we offer region selection and data locality guarantees at contract scope with audit logs showing access geography
[05:50] Marco Diaz: curious about dev workflow: how do you ensure secure SDLC? code scanning, dependency scanning, and pre-merge gating?
[05:57] Samir Cortez: we run SAST and DAST pipeline gates for critical services, SCA for dependencies, and require signed commits for production merges. we can share our pipeline overview and toolchain list — we also rotate secrets via vault and rotate at 90-day cadence by default
[06:13] Lena Gomez: secret rotation — do you integrate with our Vault and can you use external secret brokers?
[06:18] Priya Nambiar: yes, we support external secret managers (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) via our secret-proxy pattern; keys are mounted ephemeral for jobs and never persisted in plain text in our control plane logs
[06:29] Ethan Ross: remediation SLAs — you mentioned base numbers, are those negotiable in an enterprise contract? we will likely want a tighter window for critical
[06:36] Jordan Lee: yes negotiable — we can offer a 48-hour contractual remediation SLA for critical if Blue Moor opts into a dedicated pod and a support tier that includes a security war room channel
[06:46] Amina Patel: about notification — how do we get alerted about a new critical finding? email is not sufficient, we want a PagerDuty or webhook to our ticketing system
06:55] Priya Nambiar: accepted. we have integrations with PagerDuty and can open a ticket via webhook to Jira or ServiceNow and create an SCC channel for ongoing incidents
[07:05] Marco Diaz: I want to confirm patch process for the container runtime finding — is there a risk to rolling a runtime update across GPUs?
[07:12] Samir Cortez: we use a staged kernel/drivers validation in our infra images and test on a subset of nodes; runtime upgrades go through canaries and hardware-compat tests to minimize GPU reprovision risks
[07:25] Ethan Ross: glossary note — a few terms in the report were mis-typed, like "kay vee cache" instead of KV cache in one paragraph, and "Redwood Inference" got transcribed as "Redwood Insistence" — just FYI
[07:34] Jordan Lee: yeah apologies for that, the PDF has the corrected naming, we'll send a clean version
[07:39] Amina Patel: last thing from compliance perspective — retention of audit logs for 7 years is our baseline, can Redwood support that for exported logs?
[07:47] Priya Nambiar: we can export long-term archives to your S3 or object store and set lifecycle to 7 years; hosted can do it with an enterprise add-on
[07:58] Lena Gomez: will the log exports include request/response payloads? we prefer sanitized traces — not full payloads
[08:05] Samir Cortez: by default we limit payloads in audit logs, include metadata and hashes. we can enable full trace capture for specific flows if you require it for debugging, but it is opt-in and will be encrypted and routed to your vault
[08:19] Marco Diaz: ok good. can we also get an SLA on evidence delivery — sometimes vendors give the report and then take weeks to provide proof of fix
[08:26] Jordan Lee: yes, actionable evidence will be delivered per the tracker timeline; we'll commit to weekly status updates for the first four weeks post-report and assign a single point of contact
[08:37] Amina Patel: final ask: can Redwood map the pen test findings to our control set? we'll send our control list and expect a mapping back
[08:44] Priya Nambiar: absolutely, we'll map to your controls and also indicate compensating controls where remediation is not immediate
[08:51] Jordan Lee: great — to recap quickly, we'll: 1) upload a redacted pen test report and remediation tracker by 12/09, 2) share KMS/HSM integration runbook and Terraform examples by 12/14, 3) schedule a technical deep dive week of 12/15 focused on KMS and patching runbooks, 4) exchange SOC2/ISO docs over secure channel by 12/11. any U/X changes or follow-ups?
[09:16] Amina Patel: no, that covers it. thanks everyone
[09:19] Lena Gomez: thank you, appreciate the clarity
[09:21] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and the tracker

End of meeting

Notes about transcript quality: automatic transcription occasionally conflated acronyms and numbers; manual redaction required for internal IPs and management-plane asset names.
